A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same DMILO/DMILO-PGD study. Their text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, memory/runtime measurements, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds MGPS/DCPS comparison results in Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: Both retain the same intermediate-layer optimization, sparse deviations, forward-operator-guided PGD, and blind-deblurring procedures. Added initial-iterate superscripts in Algorithms 1–2 clarify notation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain CelebA, FFHQ, LSUN-bedroom, and ImageNet coverage with the same super-resolution, inpainting, linear deblurring, nonlinear deblurring, and blind-deblurring tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated MGPS and DCPS comparators throughout Tables 2–4, covering super-resolution, inpainting, Gaussian deblurring, and motion deblurring. This substantially expands the main linear-task comparisons. Existing comparators and the nonlinear and appendix comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The reported sample counts, image resolution, degradation settings, observation noise, metrics, and optimization budgets remain unchanged. The added baseline comparisons introduce no documented protocol revision.

E4.justification: The projection-strategy illustration, last-timestep analysis, sparse-deviation ablation, and memory/runtime comparison including gradient checkpointing are retained. Appendix C.2–C.4 and Tables 9–11 contain the same analyses and results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or empirical error bars. The reported Gaussian noise standard deviation describes observation corruption, not uncertainty in experimental outcomes.

E6.justification: New MGPS/DCPS results in Tables 2–4 materially change rankings while retained methods' scores stay unchanged. In Table 2, MGPS's FFHQ inpainting PSNR of 35.41 exceeds DMILO-PGD's 34.62, overturning its previous lead. In Table 4, DCPS beats DMILO on FFHQ and ImageNet FID. Table 3 also incorrectly changes the FFHQ SSIM comparison margin from 0.008 to -0.008 despite unchanged underlying scores of 0.852 and 0.844.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, assumptions, S-REC definition, Theorem 4.4, and Appendix A proof are retained without substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about reducing memory demands, mitigating suboptimal convergence, extending the generator range, and achieving strong reconstruction performance.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 softens superiority to outperforming or achieving comparable performance. Section 5.2 changes motion-deblurring leadership from all metrics to most metrics. Existing mechanism explanations, kernel-size qualification, blind-deblurring limitations, and initialization discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a DMILO code-repository link in the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. Existing implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and preprocessing disclosures remain unchanged; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds six references: Chen et al. (2025), Janati et al. (2024, 2025), Moufad et al. (2025), and Zhang et al. (2024, 2025b). The related-work taxonomy and positioning relative to DMPlug, ILO, and PGD remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized wording and notation corrections, revised comparison sentences, a code-availability sentence, and an acknowledgment. The section sequence and overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2–4 gain baseline rows and revised ranking emphasis. Existing figures and algorithms shift positions as the text reflows. The ten figure images and appendix displays are retained, without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added baselines make the linear-task evaluation more informative and expose metric-specific weaknesses, accompanied by more cautious interpretations. The code link improves reproducibility information. These benefits outweigh the isolated new SSIM-margin sign error in Table 3, while the methods, theory, and appendix analyses remain stable.
